evals.name: denied-mid-task
evals.prompt: ok so i'm halfway through a fix in ~/acme-console and claude just refused to run `git switch fix/login-redirect` - it said another session (a3f91c2b, active 3m ago) is writing in this checkout and would lose the files it's mid-edit on. i do actually have another terminal open in there doing the billing migration so thats fair enough. what do i do? i need this fix on its own branch, branched off development not main. give me the exact commands
evals.expected_output: A recovery that uses EnterWorktree (not cd), creates the worktree off the right base with git first because worktree.baseRef cannot name a branch, does not reach for the bypass env var, and leaves the worktree in place so the diff is findable.
assertions: Recommends EnterWorktree as the way to move into the worktree
Warns against cd-ing into the worktree instead of entering it, or explains that entering is what gets enforcement
Creates the worktree with git so it can branch off development, rather than relying on claude --worktree / worktree.baseRef
Does not present disabling the guard (bypass env var) as the fix
Says the worktree stays on disk / names where the operator will find the work

evals.name: four-agents-one-folder
evals.prompt: planning to point 4 agents at ~/acme-console tomorrow morning: two writing code (one on search, one on the invoice export), one doing a code review of the branch i pushed last night, and one just reading through the docs to answer my questions. it's all one folder. how do i set them up so they don't trash each other? and roughly what's this going to cost me vs just doing it myself in one session
evals.expected_output: Read-only agents share the checkout; the two writers get isolation; work is partitioned by area; the cost answer identifies context multiplication rather than checkouts as the expense.
assertions: Says the reviewer and the docs reader do NOT need their own worktree
Says the two writing agents need isolation (a worktree each, or isolation: worktree on the subagent)
Says to partition the work by area/files rather than by layer
Identifies re-read context (CLAUDE.md, docs, rediscovered code) as what multiplies with N agents, and recommends scoped briefs
Does not claim the worktrees themselves are the main cost

evals.name: parallel-tickets
evals.prompt: just ran /to-tickets and it published 6 issues to github for acme/console. #12 and #13 are independent, #14 is blocked by #12, #15 and #16 are blocked by #13, #17 is blocked by everything. can i run 3 claude sessions in ~/acme-console and have them chew through these with /implement? write it up as a runbook i can follow
evals.expected_output: A runbook that reads the repo's tracker config, works the frontier (only 2 tickets are startable), claims by assignment, isolates per session, chooses the base before invoking /implement, and closes tickets to unblock dependents.
assertions: Identifies that only #12 and #13 can start, so the frontier supports 2 concurrent sessions and not 3
Says to claim a ticket by assigning it before building, so two agents cannot take the same one
Uses the repo's configured tracker (docs/agents/issue-tracker.md / gh) rather than inventing a workflow
Says one ticket per session and that /implement commits to the current branch, so the branch and tree are chosen before invoking it
Says to close each ticket when done because that is what unblocks its dependents
Warns against git stash (shared across worktrees) or blind staging
